subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` remain as an operator-selected break-glass mode, be hardened with additional CSRF/DNS-rebinding checks, or be removed with migration handling?
rationale: The code disproves the simplest attacker-Origin reproduction, but the remaining behavior intentionally weakens a Gateway security boundary and any removal would affect documented operator configuration.

options.title: Harden break-glass mode
options.body: Keep the flag only if additional same-host/DNS-rebinding defenses and focused HTTP/WebSocket origin tests are added.

options.title: Remove the flag
options.body: Delete the fallback and add compatibility-aware doctor/docs handling for users who intentionally enabled it.

options.title: Accept current policy
options.body: Leave the flag as a documented dangerous mode and rely on the existing critical audit finding for non-loopback deployments.

recommendation.title: Harden break-glass mode
recommendation.body: Keep the flag only if additional same-host/DNS-rebinding defenses and focused HTTP/WebSocket origin tests are added.

likelyOwner.reason: The current origin-check and audit paths plus the related trusted-proxy Origin hardening history point most directly to this owner for the security-boundary decision.
